predictions.label: V
predictions.reason: Producer acquires tool before source pickup (LONG), places at buffer, departs, signals ready; consumer waits ready, carries with receipt, clears ready after move, releases at target, departs; empty_0 signaled by i==0 consumer and waited/cleared by i==1 producer; serial checks for D3; final moves to homes. But buffer_0/buffer_1 are the same capacity-one buffer and the code never ensures the first item is removed before the second placement—producer for i=1 only waits empty_0 (signaled after consumer i=0 completes), which does serialize. However, tool is released in finally after buffer_lock release, but the finally block spans lines 17-26, meaning if acquire of buffer_lock at line 18 fails, tool_owned is still true and tool is released. Terminal events: ready_0 and ready_1 are cleared by consumer (line 34), empty_0 is cleared by producer i=1 (line 12). All events cleared. Resources: buffer_lock released by both arms; tool released in finally. Terminal poses reached. The main issue is that the approach sequence for LEFT source_1 requires start_pose left_wait, but producer moves to source_1 from left_wait (line 8 move to source_i after acquiring tool at left_home or left_wait). For i=0, LEFT starts at left_home, moves to source_0—matches approach. For i=1, after i=0 cycle, LEFT is at left_wait (line 21), acquires tool, moves to source_1—matches approach start_pose left_wait. This appears satisfied. Label V because the code does not implement the D3 serial check correctly: it performs checks inside the try block after acquiring buffer_lock (line 18) but before moving to buffer, while the SPEC requires checks before entering buffer—this is a structural violation of required_order.
